title: Prove Orbit as Yazelix Nova's durable terminal runtime
description: Deliver the evidence needed to decide whether Orbit can replace the session and multiplexer layer beneath Mars. This epic authorizes only the agreed Linux-first, local, one-session, one-client experiment. Completion requires a libghostty feasibility result, a real PTY vertical slice, terminal-state convergence proof, a minimal native client, focused protocol hardening, opt-in Yazelix dogfood, an architecture checkpoint, and an explicit graduation decision. It does not authorize multiplayer, remote transport, Zellij compatibility, layouts, tabs, plugins, a configuration framework, daemon-restart persistence, or wholesale reuse from Mars Next.

title: Prove the libghostty attachment model
description: Test the riskiest Orbit assumption before architecture grows: one Rust program can own headless libghostty terminal state, derive a coherent attachment snapshot, and initialize another libghostty state that remains convergent when both receive the same subsequent PTY bytes. Use deterministic VT input on Linux and the smallest executable proof. Record the exact APIs, dependency boundary, and observed limitations in this bead. Acceptance: the proof builds and runs; authoritative state can be inspected meaningfully; snapshot plus ordered tail produces the same visible terminal state in a second instance, or the missing API is identified precisely with reproducible evidence. Stop for a user decision before adding a libghostty fork, compatibility layer, or substantial wrapper.

title: Build one real headless detachable PTY session
description: Implement the smallest headless Orbit slice after the libghostty model is proven. Orbit owns one real PTY shell and authoritative terminal state, listens on one local Unix socket, permits exactly one active client, forwards client input and resize events, keeps the child alive across client disconnect, and defines explicit child-exit and server-shutdown behavior. Begin with focused lifecycle and framing checks. Acceptance: a subprocess-level check starts a real shell, attaches a diagnostic client, exchanges input and output, disconnects without killing the shell, reconnects, and observes continued state; a second concurrent attach is rejected deterministically. Keep one Rust package and binary unless evidence requires another owner.

title: Prove gap-free terminal convergence after reattach
description: Create the defining automated Orbit contract test. Start a real PTY program, establish known terminal state, disconnect the client, produce output while detached, reattach from a coherent snapshot boundary, then continue live output. Compare the client libghostty state with Orbit authoritative state at meaningful checkpoints. Acceptance: the test detects missing, duplicated, or reordered bytes; proves snapshot and tail have no race window; covers output during detachment; and passes repeatedly without timing sleeps as correctness mechanisms. Compare user-visible terminal state rather than implementation trivia.

title: Add the minimal native Orbit client
description: Add only the graphical surface needed to dogfood the proven session contract: one native window, libghostty rendering, keyboard input, resize propagation, attach, and detach. Orbit remains the experimental project name; Mars naming is deferred until graduation. Acceptance: the client attaches to the real headless session, renders its reconstructed state, continues live rendering and input, resizes coherently, and can exit without terminating the PTY. Exclude tabs, panes, settings UI, decorations, frosted glass, configuration, shell integration, and compatibility work.

title: Harden the one-client attachment boundary
description: Challenge the minimal implementation at the boundaries most likely to invalidate the architecture. Cover client failure during rapid output and escape sequences, alternate-screen applications, Unicode and combining characters, resize while attached and detached, client crash, PTY process exit, server shutdown, and an attach attempt while a client is active. Acceptance: focused checks or reproducible dogfood prove defined behavior for each case; no byte gap or duplication is observed; failures are explicit rather than hangs; and weak or redundant tests are not retained. Do not broaden into multiplayer, remote transport, daemon restart recovery, or general protocol extensibility.

title: Dogfood Orbit through an opt-in Yazelix path
description: Integrate the proven Orbit slice into Yazelix Nova behind an explicit opt-in path such as yzx orbit while preserving the current Mars and Zellij default. Package the exact Orbit revision through the Yazelix Nix flake and verify the changed runtime surface. Acceptance: the opt-in command launches Orbit in a fresh session; the normal yzx path is unchanged; flake checks, package build, and temporary-profile installation pass; and fresh-session dogfood covers a shell, Neovim, Yazi, a full-screen TUI, and a long-running process across client detach and reattach. Record concrete failures and friction in this bead rather than expanding scope during dogfood.

title: Choose Orbit's post-experiment ownership boundaries
description: After opt-in dogfood, review evidence with the user and decide what, if anything, Orbit should own beyond the initial one-session contract. Consider multiple independent sessions, persistent scrollback, pane or workspace topology, daemon-restart recovery, shell integration, and richer terminal protocols as separate choices. Acceptance: each choice records observed user need, proposed single owner, cheapest proving check, expected LOC and complexity, and a clear accept, reject, or defer decision. Do not create implementation beads for an option before the user accepts it. Record important rejected alternatives here.

title: Decide whether Orbit graduates beneath Mars
description: Make an explicit go or no-go decision after the contract, native client, hardening, and fresh Yazelix dogfood are complete. A go decision means Orbit has earned the session-runtime role and the graphical client may graduate to the Mars name; it does not itself authorize removing the existing Mars or Zellij runtime. Acceptance: summarize contract evidence, known limitations, LOC, dependency and maintenance cost, dogfood results, and remaining P0 or P1 risks; obtain the user decision; then create only the accepted promotion or retirement beads. A no-go decision records why and what should be retained or deleted.
